unverified_summary: Nothing on this page is publisher confirmed as currently redeemable, so every candidate is listed as awaiting editor verification. That is not a gap in the research. Roblox publishes no list of active promo codes anywhere, and its own support article says only that codes may expire at any time, so the sole evidence that would upgrade a row is a redemption on a fresh account. We could not run that test before publication. We also could not confirm the exact punctuation in six older codes that carry asterisks, dollar signs or exclamation marks, nor whether the Roblox redeem box treats letter case as significant. No live People Also Ask block could be captured for the focus keyword, so the question coverage was built from competitor FAQ sets and autocomplete instead.

fakes.claim: Promo codes worth 2000, 10000 or 22500 free Robux
fakes.why_wrong: Roblox has never issued a promo code that awards Robux. Its own support article states there is no such thing as free Robux offers, tricks or codes, and that anyone claiming otherwise is running a scam.
fakes.origin: Autocomplete driven spam pages and video thumbnails. Roblox promo codes 2000 Robux is one of the highest volume searches on this term and every result for it is fabricated.

fakes.claim: Robux generator sites that ask for your username and a human verification step
fakes.why_wrong: There is no API that mints Robux. The verification step exists to harvest a password, a phone number or an affiliate payout. Roblox treats these as a Terms of Use violation and warns that they take accounts and items.
fakes.origin: Ad networks and reuploaded YouTube tutorials. This page will not name or link them, because naming a scam host is a referral.

fakes.claim: Codes revived from the expired list and presented as new
fakes.why_wrong: Once a Roblox promo code is deactivated it cannot be redeemed again. Retyping TWEETROBLOX or FREENGNBOI returns an invalid code message. The expired archive on this page exists so you can check a code against it before wasting the attempt.
fakes.origin: Creators padding a list for views. GamesRadar names this practice directly in its own guide.

fakes.claim: A promo code that unlocks Roblox Premium or a subscription for free
fakes.why_wrong: The same Roblox support article that covers Robux generators covers subscription generators, and rules both out. Premium is a paid subscription and no code grants it.
fakes.origin: Generator sites that ran out of Robux angles and moved to subscriptions.

fakes.claim: Codes typed into a specific Roblox game presented as platform promo codes
fakes.why_wrong: In-experience codes are issued by that game's developer and are typed into a code box inside the game. They will never work on the Roblox redeem page, and a platform code will never work in a game's code box.
fakes.origin: Aggregators that merge both kinds into one list without saying which is which. It is the single most common reason a reader reports a code as broken.

changes.what: Page published with the full archive of platform promo codes, live candidates and dead
Redemption path recorded as the Roblox redeem page after the older promo codes path was found to redirect there
SPIDERCOLA listed as the only site wide code any source still reports as live, held at Unverified pending a redemption test
Mansion of Wonder and Island of Move experiences confirmed live and first party, so their in-experience codes stay listed

next_change.pattern: Roblox now releases platform promo codes only alongside a retail tie in, a regional launch or a milestone, with no advance notice. The last new site wide codes landed with a regional launch and lasted about a year before expiring. Long gaps between codes are the norm rather than a sign the page is stale.
